_why: WSG-6. Three different states returned `start_fresh` and only two of them mean it: no file, and a file that parsed and holds no record for this feature. A file that EXISTS and could not be read is neither -- the store may hold dozens of records and a live owner for this very feature, and `start_fresh` tells the caller to initialise over it. The incident that filed this was a state file that vanished with the cause undetermined; an unreadable file is the half a tool can defend against. An ABSENT file still answers start_fresh deliberately, so both directions are mutated.

mutations.name: an-unreadable-state-file-reads-as-nothing-claimed-again
mutations._mechanism: The defect itself. A truncated write over a populated store routes a second session to initialise a feature the first is actively working, and nothing downstream can tell that from a genuinely new feature.

mutations.name: an-absent-file-becomes-a-false-alarm
mutations._mechanism: The over-firing direction, which matters as much: a feature that was never started is the COMMON case, and answering cannot_judge there makes every first resume a false alarm. An alert that is usually wrong is ignored, and then the real one is ignored too.

mutations.name: the-token-leaves-the-decision-table
mutations._mechanism: A token nobody documented is one every caller's enumeration misclassifies by whatever its default is. An operator who hits cannot_judge with no prescribed action falls back to guessing, and the obvious guess is to treat it like start_fresh.
mutations.find: | `cannot_judge` | The state file EXISTS and could not be read
mutations.replace: | `cannot_judged` | The state file EXISTS and could not be read
